summary: Longhorn correctly detects the read-only filesystem and requests a remount by deleting the workload pod, but on a single node the replacement pod can begin NodePublishVolume before the old pod has completed NodeUnpublishVolume. The old read-only pod mount therefore still participates in the same-node mount topology while the new pod is published. The CSI log shows the replacement publish observing the global staging mount as read-only/corrupt before the previous pod mount is unpublished. Recreating pods without waiting for the old mount to be cleaned up thus preserves the read-only state and triggers repeated remount/requeue churn rather than recovery.
